Rashi on Chullin 94a:10:1.hebrew: לא יסרהב - לא יפציר בו, הואיל ויודע שלא יעשה, משום דגונב דעתו להחזיק לו טובה בחנם, כסבור שמן הלב מסרהב לו כן:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:10:1.english: He should not importune - He should not press him, since he knows that he will not do [so], because he deceives him into feeling grateful to him for nothing, thinking that he is importuning him sincerely:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:1.hebrew: ולא יפתח לו כו' - כל חביותיהם מגופות היו, וכשבא אדם חשוב אצלו, פותח לו חבית להשקותו יין חזק. ואם מכר חבית לחנוני שלמה ועדיין היא אצלו, לא יפתחנה לאורח הבא לו, מפני שגונב לבו להחזיק לו טובה חנם; כסבור זה: הפסד גדול נפסד ע"י, שהרי תשאר חבית זו חסרה ותתקלקל יינה — וזה ימסרנה מיד לחנוני שימכרנה לו:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:1.english: And one may not open [barrels] for him, etc. - All their barrels were sealed, and when an important person comes to him, he opens a barrel for him to give him strong wine to drink. And if he sold a whole barrel to a storekeeper and it is still with him [in the seller's possession], he should not open it for a guest who comes to him, because he deceives him into feeling grateful to him for nothing; [for] this [guest] thinks: "A great loss was suffered on my account, since this barrel will remain incomplete and its wine will spoil" — whereas this [host] will immediately hand it over to the storekeeper to sell it for him:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:2.hebrew: אא"כ הודיעו - "מכרתיה לחנוני, ואיני נפסד":
Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:2.english: Unless he notifies him - [telling him,] "I have sold it to a storekeeper, and I suffer no loss [by opening it]:"

Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:3.hebrew: לא יביא לו פך ריקן ויאמר לו סוך שמן - מפני שיודע בו שאינו סך, וגונב דעתו, כסבור שיש בו שמן:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:3.english: He may not bring him an empty jug and say to him, "Anoint [yourself with] oil" - because he knows of him that he will not anoint [himself], and he deceives him, [for the guest] thinks that there is oil in it:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:4.hebrew: ואם בשביל כבודו - של אורח, להודיע לבריות שחביב הוא עליו, מותר:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:11:4.english: But if [it is] for his honor - [that] of the guest, to let people know that he is dear to him, it is permitted:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:13:1.english: That rattles - [Meaning,] partially empty. [This is forbidden] because this [mourner] thinks that it is full:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:13:2.english: That he misleads him - he deceives him:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:13:3.hebrew: ואם יש שם חבר עיר - חבורות עיר, שיש שם רבים, וזה מתכוין להחשיב את האבל בעיניהן, שיאמרו: כמה חשוב זה, שזה מכבדו כ"כ:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:13:3.english: But if there is a ḥever ir [a crowd of townspeople] there - [This refers to] groups of townspeople, where many [people] are present, and this [visitor] intends to make the mourner appear important in their eyes, so that they will say: How important is this [man], that this [person] honors him so much.

Rashi on Chullin 94a:13:4.english: It is permitted - because human dignity is great:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:14:1.hebrew: סנדל - של עור בהמה שמתה חיה מאליה, אין עורה חזק כשל בריאה שחוטה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:14:1.english: A sandal - [Made] of the hide of an animal that died on its own; its hide is not as strong as [that] of a healthy slaughtered [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:14:2.english: A live slaughtered [animal] - [Meaning] a healthy slaughtered [animal]:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:14:3.hebrew: הסכנה - שמא מחמת נשיכת נחש מתה, והארס נבלע בעור:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:14:3.english: The danger - Perhaps [the animal] died from a snakebite, and the venom was absorbed into the hide:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:15:1.hebrew: ושמן צף על פיה - כסבור שהכל שמן, ומזמן עליו אורחים, ובטוח שיש לו שמן הרבה לצרכם:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:15:1.english: With oil floating at its mouth - [The recipient] thinks that all of it is oil, and invites guests on account of it, confident that he has plenty of oil for their needs:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:15:2.english: And he hanged himself - because he had nothing to feed them, and was ashamed before them:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:17:1.english: That [he] encloses - [This means] shutting in, as in "and he fenced it in" (Isaiah 5):

Rashi on Chullin 94a:19:1.hebrew: שלימה אין צריך ליטול - מפני שניכר שלא ניטל, והאוכלה נוטלו:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:19:1.english: [If it is] whole, he does not need to remove [the sciatic nerve] - because it is recognizable that it has not been removed, and the one who eats it removes it:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:19:2.english: And in [the case of] a gentile, whether whole, etc. - Later [the Gemara] explains it:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:1.hebrew: חתוכה נמי לישדר - עם גידה, דליכא למיחש שמא ימכרנה לישראל, דהא לא זבני מיניה, דחיישינן לטרפה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:1.english: Let him also send [it] cut up - with its [sciatic] nerve, since there is no [reason] to be concerned that he might sell it to a Jew, for [Jews] do not buy from him, as we are concerned about [it being] a tereifah:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:2.hebrew: אלא במקום שמכריזין - שישראל מותר ליקח שם באותו מקום מן העובד כוכבים כיון שלא הכריזו, דלמאי ניחוש לה? הטבחים ישראלים הם, ולטרפה ליכא למיחש, דהא לא הכריזו היום:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:2.english: Rather, in a place where they announce - [meaning] that a Jew is permitted to buy [meat] there, in that place, from an idolater since they did not make an announcement — for what should we be concerned about regarding it? The butchers are Jews, and as for [it being] a tereifah, there is no reason to be concerned, since they did not announce [one] today.

Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:3.hebrew: שלימה נמי לא לישדר ליה - עד שיטול גידה, דאע"פ שמקומו ניכר, איכא למיחש דלמא חתיך לה עובד כוכבים ומזבין, וסבור זה שנטל גידה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:1:3.english: He should not send him even a whole [thigh] - until he removes its [sciatic] nerve; for even though its place is recognizable, there is [reason] to be concerned lest the gentile cut it up and sell [it], and this [buyer] will think that its nerve was removed:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:20:1.hebrew: אין מוכרין טרפה לעובד כוכבים - בסתם, אא"כ הודיעו שהיא טרפה, דתו ליכא גניבת דעת. ובמקום שאין מכריזין, דליכא למיחש לשמא ימכרנה לישראל, או במקום שמכריזין וביום שהכריזו — הכי מתוקמא לקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:20:1.english: One may not sell a tereifah to a gentile - [This prohibition applies] when [sold] without specification, unless one informed him that it is a tereifah, for then there is no deception. And [selling is permitted only] in a place where they do not announce [non-kosher meat], where there is no concern lest he sell it to a Jew, or in a place where they do announce and on a day when they announced — so it is established below:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:3:1.hebrew: חיתוכא דעובד כוכבים - בירך, אינו עשוי כשל ישראל, שהוא פורעה כדרך שהגיד מונח. ועל דא סמיך רבי בשולח ירך לחבירו על יד עובד כוכבים, ולא עשה בה חותם, דכשרה היא אם היא חתוכה כדרך שישראל חותכה אחר חטיטת הגיד; אבל באבר אחר, שחיתוך עובד כוכבים וחיתוך ישראל שוין בו, אסור עד שיהא בו חותם:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:3:1.english: The cutting of a gentile - in the thigh, it is not made like [that] of a Jew, who slits it open along the path where the [sciatic] nerve lies. And on this Rabbi relies regarding one who sends a thigh to his fellow via a gentile and did not place a seal on it, that it is kosher if it is cut in the way a Jew cuts it after excising the [sciatic] nerve; but with another limb, in which a gentile's cutting and a Jew's cutting are identical, it is forbidden unless it has a seal:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:4:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא במקום שאין מכריזין - ודקשיא לך: חתוכה נמי לישדר, דהא לא זבין לה ישראל — גזירה שמא יתננה לו בפני ישראל, ואותו הרואה שזה נתנה לו לוקח הימנו, וכסבור ניטל גידה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:4:1.english: And if you wish, say [it is] in a place where they do not announce - And [as for] what was difficult for you — [namely,] let him send a cut-up [thigh] as well, since a Jew will not buy it — [it is] a decree lest he give it to him in the presence of [another] Jew, and that [person] who sees that this [Jew] gave it to him will buy [it] from him, thinking [that] its sinew has been removed:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:5:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - טעמא דמתני', דאמר חתוכה לא לישדר עם גידה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:5:1.english: And if you wish, say - [This is] the reason of the Mishnah, which states [that] one should not send a cut-up [thigh] with its [sciatic] nerve:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:5:2.hebrew: משום דגונב דעתו - דעובד כוכבים כסבור שישראל זה אוהבו מאד, שתקנה וטרח בה ליטול גידה עד שנראית לעצמו, ואח"כ נתנה לו, והוא לא נטלו, ונמצא מחזיק לו טובה חנם:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:5:2.english: Because he deceives him - For the gentile thinks that this Jew loves him very much, that he prepared it and exerted himself with it to remove its [sciatic] nerve until it was fit for himself, and afterward gave it to him — whereas he did not remove it, and it turns out that [the gentile] feels grateful to him for nothing:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:6:1.english: A ferry - A wide boat in which they cross the river:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:6:2.english: Compensate the ferryman - Give his fee to the owner of the ferry:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:7:1.hebrew: במר דשחוטה - בחילוף שחוטה, בחזקת שחוטה, וחבירו בבכורות (דף ל.): "ההוא טבחא דמזבין תרבא דאטמא במר דכנתא". ולי נראה דלשון תמורה הוא. דהאי דטרפה לאו דוקא, דטרפה בשחוטה לא מיחלפא, אלא כלומר: טרפה שחוטה נתן לו במר דכשרה שחוטה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:7:1.english: As a slaughtered [kosher] one [bemar deshechuta] - [Meaning] in place of a slaughtered [kosher] one, [i.e.,] with the presumption of being a slaughtered [kosher] one; and its parallel [appears] in [tractate] Bekhorot (30a): "A certain butcher who sold [forbidden] fat of the hip in place of [permitted] fat of the kanta." But to me it appears that [bemar] is an expression of exchange [temurah]. For this [term] "tereifa" is not [meant] literally [as an unslaughtered bird], since an [unslaughtered] tereifa cannot be mistaken for a slaughtered one; rather, [Abaye] means to say: he gave him a slaughtered tereifa in exchange for a slaughtered kosher [chicken]:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:7:2.english: And he gave him diluted wine to drink - and the idolater thought that the wine was undiluted:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:8:1.hebrew: וכי מכללא מאי - מה לנו אי איתמר מכלל אי בפירוש? הא מהא כללא שפיר שמעינן, ואמאי אשמעינן גמרא דלאו בפירוש אתמר, ומה יש לנו לגמגם בכלל זה:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:8:1.english: And if [it was derived] by inference, what [of it]? - What does it matter to us whether it was stated by inference or explicitly? After all, from this inference we learn [it] well, and why did the Gemara inform us that it was not stated explicitly, and what [reason] do we have to cast doubt on this inference:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:8:2.hebrew: למ"ד טרפה הואי - איכא למימר דלאו משום גניבות דעת איקפיד, אלא משום דאשהייה גביה עד השתא:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:8:2.english: According to the one who said it was a tereifa - One can say that it was not because of deceiving [the gentile] that he became angry, rather because he kept it with him until now:

Rashi on Chullin 94a:9:1.hebrew: אנפקא חייא משמע - משום יקרא דידיה איקפיד, שעבר על דבריו:
Rashi on Chullin 94a:9:1.english: Anpaka implies undiluted [wine] - It was because of his own honor that [Shmuel] became angry, because [the attendant] disobeyed his words:

Tosafot on Chullin 94a:3:1.hebrew: חיתוכא דעובד כוכבים מידע ידיע - פירש בקונטרס: דחיתוך דעובד כוכבים בירך אינו עשוי כשל ישראל, שהוא פורעה כדרך שהגיד מונח, ועל דא סמיך רבי בשולח ירך על יד עובד כוכבים לחבירו ולא עשה בו חותם, דכשרה היא אם חתוכה כדרך שישראל חותכה אחר חטיטת גיד, עכ"ל. ותימה: דאם כן, לוקמיה אף כשאין מכריזין, וחתוכה לא לישדר ליה, דלמא אתי ליזדבוני לישראל! דכיון דחיתוך דישראל מידע ידיע, לא יחוש ישראל הבא לקנותה שמא טרפה היא, דאם כן למה פתחה וחתכה כדרך שעושין כדי ליטול הגיד? וכי תימא דחייש ישראל שמא אחר כך נודע לו שהיא טרפה — דא"כ, מטעם זה נאסור בשולח ירך לחבירו ע"י עובד כוכבים, שמא נזדמנה לעובד כוכבים ירך אחרת שלא נודע לישראל שהיתה טרפה עד אחר שניטל גידה, והחליפה בזאת! וי"ל: דכולי האי לא חיישינן, דלא שכיח שיזדמן כך ליד עובד כוכבים; אבל היכא דישראל שלח לעובד כוכבים, חייש ישראל במקום שאין מכריזין, אע"פ שניטל גידה, דלמא דלכך שלחה לעובד כוכבים לפי שנודע לו אחר ניקור דטרפה היא:
Tosafot on Chullin 94a:3:1.english: The cutting of a gentile is recognizable - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: That the cutting of a gentile on a thigh is not done like that of a Jew, who opens it along the path where the [sciatic] nerve lies; and upon this Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] relied when sending a thigh to his colleague via a gentile without placing a seal on it — for it is kosher if it is cut in the manner that a Jew cuts it after excising the nerve. Thus far his wording. And this is puzzling: if so, let [the Gemara] establish [the Mishnah] even where they do not announce, and [say that] one may not send a cut [thigh] to him [a gentile], lest he come to sell [it] to a Jew! For since a Jew's cutting is recognizable, a Jew who comes to buy it will not suspect that perhaps it is a tereifa — for if [it were], why did [the Jewish butcher] open it and cut it in the manner they do in order to remove the nerve? And if you should say that a Jew would suspect that perhaps it became known to [the butcher] afterward that it was a tereifa — if so, for this [same] reason we should forbid sending a thigh to one's colleague via a gentile, lest the gentile happened to have another thigh that was not known to a Jew to be a tereifa until after its nerve was removed, and he exchanged it for this one! And one can answer: We are not concerned to that extent, because it is uncommon that such a [thigh] would happen to come into a gentile's hand; however, where a Jew sent [a thigh] to a gentile, a Jew [buying from the gentile] is concerned in a place where they do not announce — even though its nerve was removed — [that] perhaps this is why he sent it to the gentile, because it became known to him after porging that it was a tereifa:

Tosafot on Chullin 94a:7:1.hebrew: טרפה הואי ויהבה ניהליה במר דשחוטה - וא"ת: לעולם אימא לך דמותר לגנוב דעתו של עובד כוכבים, ואיקפד משום דאמר לו לעובד כוכבים "שחוטה היא", ואיכא למיגזר שמא יתננה לו בפני ישראל ויקנה ממנו? וי"ל: דמ"מ איכא למידק מיניה דאסור לגנוב דעתו, דאי שרי, ליכא למיחש שמא יקנה ממנו ישראל, דיחוש דלגנוב דעתו של עובד כוכבים אומר כן:
Tosafot on Chullin 94a:7:1.english: It was a tereifa and he gave it to him as though it were slaughtered - And if you say: Actually, I could tell you that it is permitted to deceive an idolater, and [Shmuel] became angry because [the attendant] said to the idolater, "It is slaughtered," and there is [reason] to decree [against it] lest he give it to him in the presence of a Jew and [the Jew] buy [it] from him? One can say: In any event, one can infer from it that it is forbidden to deceive him; for if it were permitted, there would be no [reason] to be concerned lest a Jew buy [it] from him, since [the Jew] would suspect that he is saying so [merely] to deceive the idolater:
